## Description {#details}

<p>Base struct for all "concrete attribute" deductions.</p>


<p>The abstract attribute is a minimal interface that allows the <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/structs/llvm/attributor">Attributor</a> to orchestrate the abstract/fixpoint analysis. The design allows to hide away implementation choices made for the subclasses but also to structure their implementation and simplify the use of other abstract attributes in-flight.</p>


<p>To allow easy creation of new attributes, most methods have default implementations. The ones that do not are generally straight forward, except <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#adae4d3d2e4be96b506c572fcc4a8738a">AbstractAttribute::updateImpl</a></span> which is the location of most reasoning associated with the abstract attribute. The update is invoked by the <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/structs/llvm/attributor">Attributor</a> in case the situation used to justify the current optimistic state might have changed. The <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/structs/llvm/attributor">Attributor</a> determines this automatically by monitoring the <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/structs/llvm/attributor/#a4f07dfd5d71c602655995567fe27d4a7">Attributor::getAAFor</a></span> calls made by abstract attributes.</p>


<p>The <span class="doxyComputerOutput">updateImpl</span> method should inspect the IR and other abstract attributes in-flight to justify the best possible (=optimistic) state. The actual implementation is, similar to the underlying abstract state encoding, not exposed. In the most common case, the <span class="doxyComputerOutput">updateImpl</span> will go through a list of reasons why its optimistic state is valid given the current information. If any combination of them holds and is sufficient to justify the current optimistic state, the method shall return UNCHAGED. If not, the optimistic state is adjusted to the situation and the method shall return CHANGED.</p>


<p>If the manifestation of the "concrete attribute" deduced by the subclass differs from the "default" behavior, which is a (set of) LLVM-IR attribute(s) for an argument, call site argument, function return value, or function, the <span class="doxyComputerOutput"><a href="#a1405b111f812f19e71bbe4286484ef54">AbstractAttribute::manifest</a></span> method should be overloaded.</p>


<p>NOTE: If the state obtained via <a href="#a5f3c26aaee1ca991435953c032b3fd08">getState()</a> is INVALID, thus if <a href="#a5f3c26aaee1ca991435953c032b3fd08">AbstractAttribute::getState()</a>.isValidState() returns false, no information provided by the methods of this class should be used. NOTE: The <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/structs/llvm/attributor">Attributor</a> currently has certain limitations to what we can do. As a general rule of thumb, "concrete" abstract attributes should <em>for now</em> only perform "backward" information propagation. That means optimistic information obtained through abstract attributes should only be used at positions that precede the origin of the information with regards to the program flow. More practically, information can <em>now</em> be propagated from instructions to their enclosing function, but <em>not</em> from call sites to the called function. The mechanisms to allow both directions will be added in the future. NOTE: The mechanics of adding a new "concrete" abstract attribute are described in the file comment.</p>


<p>Definition at line 3293 of file <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/include/include/llvm/include/llvm/transforms/include/llvm/transforms/ipo/attributor-h">Attributor.h</a>.</p>
